title: The Clinical Trial Data Problem
segments: Clinical trials require accurate, standardized, and traceable data.
Converting a clinical Protocol into an eCRF remains highly manual.
Teams identify required data, design fields, define validation rules, and map them to CDISC CDASH.
Even a small amendment can affect forms, mappings, and downstream analysis.

title: Introducing the Solution
segments: We created Codex Clinical Form Studio.
It is a reusable Plugin composed of specialized Skills, not a single form-generating prompt.
After a user uploads a Protocol, an Orchestrator Skill coordinates analysis, design, CDASH mapping, clinical review, testing, and deployment.
Every stage has defined input, output, and human approval.

title: GPT-5.6 and Protocol Analysis
segments: The Orchestrator invokes the Protocol Analysis Skill, while GPT-5.6 provides medical and logical reasoning.
GPT-5.6 identifies forms, fields, data types, units, required conditions, options, and validation rules, then converts them into structured YAML.
YAML becomes the single source of truth.
Clinical users can review it in a web interface instead of editing application code.

title: Clinical Editing and CDASH Mapping
segments: Clinical users modify fields, required conditions, numeric limits, and selectable options.
The Orchestrator then invokes the CDASH Mapping Skill.
GPT-5.6 evaluates each field in its Protocol context, ranks CDASH candidates, and explains its recommendations.
AI suggests, but the clinical professional makes the final mapping decision.

title: Generating an Executable eCRF
segments: After approval, the Form Generation Skill converts YAML into standardized JSON.
The JSON-to-HTML renderer generates an executable eCRF with controls, required settings, allowed values, ranges, and validation.
The form first enters a validation environment for clinical review.

title: Codex Engineering and Automated QA
segments: Codex turns the approved specification into maintainable engineering work.
The Orchestrator directs Codex to update the application, generate database migrations, create pytest and Playwright tests, and validate in a real browser.
When a test fails, Codex traces YAML, the renderer, or the application, corrects the issue, and retests.

title: Protocol Version Comparison
segments: When a new Protocol version arrives, the Version Comparison Skill compares both YAML specifications.
It identifies added, removed, and modified fields, including required conditions, validation rules, options, and CDASH mappings.
This creates a traceable record of each amendment.

title: GitHub and Deployment
segments: GPT-5.6 interprets complex Protocols and reasons about CDISC mappings.
Codex implements the application, writes tests, fixes failures, and prepares GitHub pull requests.
After clinical approval and QA, the CI/CD pipeline deploys the validated eCRF.
Codex Clinical Form Studio packages the workflow into a reusable, testable Plugin. Human approval remains required at every critical clinical decision.
